# Build decisions log

Choices builders made where mvp-spec.md v1.4 is silent, ambiguous or contradictory (pick, log, keep going). Logan signs them off at the milestone gates. A value chosen here is a named constant in code, with a comment pointing back to its row.

| Id | Spec | Question | Choice | Constant | PR | Signed off |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | 5.13, 5.14, 5.17 | The sector table with annual volatility, beta and typical payout ratio is in no CSV; `g_sector` is undefined | One shared default per value for all 42 industries (all industries already share defaults); `g_sector` is the industry's `lt` growth | `SECTOR_VOLATILITY`, `SECTOR_BETA`, `SECTOR_PAYOUT` (set in M5/M6) | Phase 0 | Logan, plan |
| D2 | all | Tie-break when the spec gives none | Lower id wins, so iteration order stays deterministic | (none) | Phase 0 | Logan, plan |
| D3 | 3 | Share counts as u32 overflow for large companies | Share counts are u64; money is f64 USD, with CSV $M, $bn and bps converted once at load | (none) | Phase 0 | Logan, plan |
| D4 | 3, 9.2 | What order are table ordinals (province, company, industry and the rest) in? | Ascending byte order of the CSV id (CO-0001 is CompanyId 0); rows born in play append. Ties to the lower id (D2) are ties to the lower ordinal | (none) | M1 | |
| D5 | 4.1 step 1, 9.1 | 4.1 applies queued controls at the start of a tick, but while paused no tick runs, so a queued Resume would never apply | `Sim::apply` applies controls at once. MVP controls change only runner state (speed, pause, skip, alerts, watchlist), never the world, so this equals applying them at the next tick's step 1 | (none) | M1 | |
| D6 | 4.1 step 4, 8 | When do alerts fire, and does a Pause alert stop a SkipTo? | Calendar alerts (Earnings day, Plan lock, Quarterly recap) fire in 4.1 step 4; alerts raised by later jobs (bankruptcy, world event) fire where raised; a Pause alert pauses after its tick. During a SkipTo, Pause alerts only notify, so the skip stops at its target. The alert notice carries its level; Off posts nothing | `AlertKind::default_level` | M1 | |
| D7 | 4.4, 8, 21.8 | How is days_to_next_phase counted, and how long is the Release phase? | Calendar days from today to the day the next phase starts. Release is the 00:00 tick only (Reaction starts 01:00), so the release tick reads 0 | `RELEASE_DAY`, `PRICE_MOVE_HOUR`, `PLAN_LOCK_DAY`, `RECAP_DAYS_BEFORE_RELEASE` | M1 | |
| D8 | 3.1, 7.3, 9.1 | Speed model and SkipTo targets | Speeds 1 to 5 run at 2 s, 1 s, 0.5 s and 0.2 s of real time per game hour and max (spec 8). A new game is paused at speed 1. SetSpeed(0) pauses; SetSpeed(1 to 5) sets the speed and resumes; Pause and Resume keep the speed; Pause or SetSpeed cancels a skip. SkipTo resumes at max speed and pauses after the first target tick strictly after now: NextRelease and NextLock the next release and lock ticks, NextRecap the next pre-quarter-end week start, MonthEnd the next 1st at 00:00 (the tick that closes the month) | `START_SPEED`, `MAX_SPEED`, `SECONDS_PER_HOUR` | M1 | |
| D9 | 3.1, 12.3 | How each RNG stream is seeded from the game seed | One ChaCha8 key from `seed_from_u64(seed)`; the streams differ by ChaCha stream number, frozen: cycle 0, growth 1, prices 2, ai 3, gen 4. Box-Muller keeps its second normal as a saved spare. Knuth's Poisson is used up to a mean of 30 | `Stream` discriminants, `POISSON_MAX_MEAN` | M1 | |
| D10 | 9.3 | Which day, month or quarter do the notices name? | DayDone the day just ended; MonthDone the month just closed; EarningsReleased the quarter just ended (2 Jan 2020 is Q4 2019); PlanLocked the calendar quarter the lock falls in. TickDone is always the last notice of a step | (none) | M1 | |
| D11 | 2.1, 3.7.2, 9.2 | Spec 2.1 says to load only the characters named as controller or owner_of_record, but 9.2 `list_characters` lists all 296: the two contradict (design fix 11) | All 296 characters load into the character table; the named-controller role is a later field | (none) | M1 | |
| D12 | 4, 7.3 | Does the first step run the 2020-01-01 00:00 jobs? | No. A tick advances the clock, then runs the jobs for the new time, so the first tick is 01:00 on 1 January 2020; the 00:00 start state is built at load (7.3: plans set and the Q1 draw made at load) | `DateTime::START` | M1 | |
| D13 | 9.1, build-plan 4.3 | What does a save hold, what does the hash cover, and what happens on load? | A save holds the whole world (static tables too, so it loads without the CSVs), the RNG positions and the controls. The state hash covers the world and the RNG positions, not the controls (they never change the world). Loading pauses the game and drops any skip; Omniscient is cleared in release builds | `SAVE_VERSION`, `HASH_FORMAT` | M1 | |
| D14 | build-plan M0.8, M7.7 | The table spike's real-GPU checks (frame time, wheel step, HiDPI clicks, resize, fonts, 10,000 rows) could not be run by screen control | Folded into M7.7: the table widget logs frame and sort times to stdout in release, and its tests cover pool sizing on resize and a 10,000-row sort; Logan checks wheel feel and HiDPI clicks by hand at the M6 + M7 gate | (none) | housekeeping | |
| D200 | 5.10, 3.7, 5.19.4, C31 | Which labor_value counts the labor units, and do startups near $1M open all five seats? | `labor_units = max(1, floor(Σ gross ÷ labor_value))` with the main industry's labor_value (one unit per company in the MVP). Seats are always the first min(5, L) labor seats; a born company follows the same rule. With the MVP defaults the smallest startup ($1M, 5.19.3) has $1M of assets and 10 labor units, so all five seats open at birth, matching 5.19.4 and C31; if data ever gave L < 5 at birth, only those seats open and the rest of the cast sit as directors (5.19.4 step 4) | `MIN_LABOR_UNITS` | F3 | |
| D201 | 5.10, 10.0.11.3 | The drop order (idle, research, enterprise, productivity) omits 50/50 stations, and says nothing when labor rises | 50/50 drops after enterprise, before productivity (it is half of each). New labor units are idle until the next plan assigns them | (none) | F3 | |
| D202 | 3.7.1 | Size band edges, draw order and trait draw of a simple character | Small under $100M, Mid from $100M, Large from $10B (edges go up). Draw order, frozen: name (sex, first name, surname), age, the six skills in column order, trait count (two with 40%), traits (uniform from the seat's list, then uniform from the rest minus the first and its opposite) | `MID_REVENUE_USD`, `LARGE_REVENUE_USD`, `TWO_TRAIT_CHANCE` | F3 | |
| D203 | 3.7.1, 3.7.2 | How a name is built from the superregion lists, and what if a unique full name cannot be found | Culture from names/country-cultures.csv, its rows in the country's superregion file (falls back to the file's first culture if missing; never happens with today's data); female 50%; first name then surname, surname first for family_first cultures, as world-gen gen.py does. Simple characters need not be unique; full characters retry up to 200 draws, then take the lowest free roman numeral suffix (" II", ...) | `FEMALE_CHANCE`, `UNIQUE_NAME_TRIES` | F3 | |
| D204 | 3.7.2, 5.19.4 | 3.7.2 says a full character's best skill is its seat's skill; 5.19.4 step 2 says it takes the open seat whose skill is its best (design fix 202). Also cash and home province draws | Each non-lead founder is cast for a seat first: uniform among the open labor seats other than the CEO (`pick_cast_seat`), and generated with that seat's skill as best; with no open seat it is a director whose best skill is any of the six. The lead founder's best is one of Finance, Operations, Persuasion, uniform. The second skill is uniform among the other five. Cash is a uniform whole-dollar draw from $100,000 to $1,000,000. Home: the HQ with 70%, else another province of the HQ country by weight (the HQ if there is none). Draw order frozen: name, age, best pick, second pick, six skills, three traits, home, cash | `HOME_AT_HQ_CHANCE`, `CASH_MIN_USD`, `CASH_MAX_USD` | F3 | |
| D205 | 5.7, 3.7 | What a closed labor seat counts in the management score, and can a shifted skill leave 0 to 30? | A labor seat that is closed (fewer labor units) or unfilled counts skill 3, like the empty Chair; a member's seat skill plus trait shifts is clamped to 0 to 30. The CMO is the 10% "other seats" weight | `EMPTY_SEAT_SKILL` | F3 | |
| D206 | 3.7.1, 10.5.1, 1.1.2 | Which trait effects reach the management score, and in which seats? | The score reads the seat skill as drawn plus the 3.7.1 shifts only: Diligent +2, Lazy -2, Ambitious +1 in any seat, Greedy -1 in the CFO seat only. 10.5.1's Deceitful -1 and Honest's confidence +1 are not in the MVP list and are not applied. The 1.1.2 skill effects (Greedy +2 Finance and so on) apply to the character's effective skills for rolls and votes (`with_trait_effects`), not to the score: counting both would double-count Diligent and lift the size means to about 37, 51, 64 against the spec's 33, 47, 60 (design fix 203); with the shifts alone they are about 34.4, 47.9, 61.4. Conditional effects (Paranoid's defense, Zealot, Narcissist) are left out | `DILIGENT_MANAGEMENT_SHIFT`, `LAZY_MANAGEMENT_SHIFT`, `AMBITIOUS_MANAGEMENT_SHIFT`, `GREEDY_CFO_MANAGEMENT_SHIFT` | F3 | |
| D207 | 6.4 | Rounding in the station split, and the CEO at L = 1 | Research is floor(10% of the labor left after P and E); the idle floor is ceil(10% of L), so idle stays at 10%+ and the 0.4 decay of 5.6 holds. At L = 1 the one station is 50/50 when coverage is 100% (even with no data inflow), else productivity; at L ≥ 2 the CEO's station is productivity | `SPLIT_VISIONARY_RESEARCH_PERCENT`, `SPLIT_MIN_IDLE_PERCENT`, `SPLIT_MIN_IDLE_FROM_LABOR`, `SPLIT_FIFTY_FIFTY_COVERAGE` | F3 | |
| D208 | 7.1, C16 | Rounding and caps in the starting loadout | Productivity stations round halves to even (Python `round`, as gen.py and validate.py do), so the engine's gross assets match company-start.csv for all 651. The PC bonus passes: pass 1 at gross for bonus 0, pass 2 at gross for pass 1's bonus, gross from pass 2's bonus (gen.py); the location bonus sits in the gross formula. Enterprise stations are capped at the labor left after productivity (a $0.12M company has one labor unit and no enterprise station; validate.py does not cap, design fix 208). The loadout reports both the bonus gross was set with and the live bonus of its stations (they differ for three companies, design fix 201) | `LOADOUT_PRODUCTIVITY_SHARE`, `LOADOUT_ENTERPRISE_DIVISOR_TB`, `LOADOUT_BONUS_PASSES` | F3 | |
| D209 | 3.8 | What "stations" and "TB stored" mean in the compute rules, and float ceilings | Stations are all labor units (every station, idle too, as validate.py uses labor). TB stored is held plus unstructured data. ceil(0.2 × stations) is the integer ceil(stations ÷ 5), so 0.2 × 15 is 3, not 4 from float error | `STATIONS_PER_EXTRA_BASE_COMPUTE`, `MIN_EXTRA_BASE_COMPUTE`, `MIN_DATA_COMPUTE` | F3 | |
| D210 | 5.9, 7.1 | Retention timing, the 1-month grace, and where the steady state is measured | Buckets are kept oldest first; the bucket made 12 months ago gets the month's conversion as its last chance, then retention drops it, leaving 12. Grace: in the first month held is below the current step, free R&D keeps the old step; the next month, if still below, it drops to the new step; any month at or above the step clears the grace. The steady state `C = rate(held) × held` is the held level after conversion and before decay (as 5.9 orders the steps); end-of-month held settles at that less C (Arrowhead 8.27 TB against 8.6, design fix 204). At load held is set to the 5.9 solution and free R&D starts at its step | `RETENTION_MONTHS`, `STEADY_STATE_ITERATIONS` | F3 | |
| D211 | 5.6 | Thresholds without float error | The idle shares compare whole units (`idle × 100 ≥ 25 × L`); the research multiplier counts decimal digits of the research units; free R&D enters rd_total as `free_rd_pct ÷ 100` | `SOME_IDLE_PERCENT`, `MUCH_IDLE_PERCENT`, `RESEARCH_MULT_STEP` | F3 | |
| D212 | 7.1, build-plan M3.8 | The Arrowhead check needs revenue and expense lines from M2 and the R&D plan from M6, which are not built | The F3 test composes the M3 functions and computes revenue, variable, fixed cash, depreciation (5.4, 5.5, 5.10) and the 6.1 and 6.3 R&D target by hand from the spec; the expected numbers (EBIT before R&D $2.35M, paid R&D $0.72M, EBIT after R&D $1.63M, 4.1%) stay when lane S swaps in its functions | (none) | F3 | |
